title: CheckpointManifest/1.1
description: Generation-level checkpoint manifest for ant-hive-world. A checkpoint is ONE generation directory, gen-<absolute_day>-<run_name>/, staged in full before any commit signal: all authoritative state files are written into a staging directory, each file's sha256 is recorded here, everything is fsynced, and THIS FILE is renamed into place last. The arrival of a checksum-valid manifest at <generation>/manifest.json IS the single authoritative commit token -- there is no separate marker file. A generation directory without a checksum-valid manifest is uncommitted, is invalid by definition, and is swept on next start. The newest committed generation is last-known-good and is NEVER auto-deleted. A generation id that already names a committed generation is a fail-closed refusal (STATUS=checkpoint-collision:<id>): never overwrite, never auto-suffix.

schema.description: Schema identifier. 1.1 is what this engine writes. 1.0 is accepted as READABLE so that a pre-learning-path generation produces an honest shape-mismatch refusal at validation stage 3 rather than a schema-shaped one; readable is not resumable.

schema_version.description: Major.minor of this manifest contract. 1.1 splits the single 1.0 architecture hash into shape_hash (mismatch = stage-3 refusal) and training_config_hash (mismatch = provenance WARN). A 1.0 manifest has neither: its legacy architecture.hash is read as the shape_hash fallback, and its training_config_hash is reported UNKNOWN -- never as matching.

code_version.description: Engine checkpoint-code version (tools/ant-hive-world/checkpoint.js CHECKPOINT_CODE_VERSION). Compared for exact equality at stage 3: a checkpoint written by different serialization code is not resumable, because the field-by-field meaning of the state files is exactly what changed.

generation_id.description: gen-<absolute_day>-<run_name>. Also the directory basename. Coordinator default; operator-overridable via the run_name it derives from.

absolute_day.description: Cumulative simulated days across the whole checkpoint lineage. One tick is one simulated day (see cloud-init/user-data MODE=turn). Equals absolute_tick; carried as its own field because the generation id is expressed in days and a future engine may decouple them.

absolute_tick.description: Cumulative tick count across the lineage, i.e. the tickIndex the NEXT tick will run with. Restored into the driver loop so the entropy-decay schedule and forced-exploration cadence continue rather than restart.

run_name.description: The run/turn name this generation was written by.

created_at.description: ISO-8601 UTC stamp. Provenance only: never read by any decision path, never compared during validation.

parent.description: Parent-generation linkage. Validation stage 5 requires: if generation_id is null this is a lineage root and lineage_depth must be 0; otherwise the named parent generation must exist locally AND its manifest_self_checksum must equal manifest_checksum here. A declared-but-absent or mismatched parent is a fail-closed refusal -- nothing in this system auto-deletes a committed generation, so a missing parent means the lineage was tampered with or truncated, which is exactly the case halt-for-repair exists for.

identity.description: Run identity and seed provenance. PROVENANCE ONLY for run_id/episode_id/arm_id/turn_index: these must not feed any RNG or decision path (verified mechanically in state-inventory.md section 4).

turn_index.description: How many driver invocations deep this lineage is. Increments once per resume.

root_seed.description: The explicit root seed this run was started from. Replaces the former Date.now()-derived seed: no run's behavior may depend on invocation time.

root_seed_source.description: How the root seed was obtained. 'generated' means crypto.randomInt (never wall-clock); 'restored' means inherited from the resumed generation.

fresh_start.description: true when the driver started without RESUME_FROM. Recorded in turn provenance so a continuity claim can never be made by silence.

architecture.description: Architecture, training-configuration and action-space descriptor. Under 1.1 there are TWO authoritative hashes with two different consequences. `shape_hash` covers layer dims, the shape the engine actually builds, the prediction-head dims, the prev_features arity and verb ORDER -- a mismatch is a stage-3 REFUSAL, because restoring parameters into a differently-shaped mind is silent corruption, not continuity. `training_config_hash` covers learning rates, the loss mask, the loss form and lag convention, the head seed-derivation constant and the resource normalizers -- a mismatch is a provenance WARN and never a refusal, because the restore is valid but the metrics are not comparable. `hash` is the sha256 over this whole object, retained for provenance and for comparison against 1.0 manifests; it is no longer the refusal criterion.

shape_hash.description: 1.1 only. Mismatch against the running engine is a stage-3 refusal. Absent on 1.0 manifests, where the legacy `hash` is read as the fallback.

training_config_hash.description: 1.1 only. Mismatch is a WARN recorded in provenance, never a refusal. Absent on 1.0 manifests, where it is reported UNKNOWN -- 'no value' and 'same value' are different facts.

world_learning.description: 1.1 only. The world mind's learning contract, in full, so a reader can see what training_config_hash is a hash OF without recomputing it. Every field here is inside training_config_hash and none is inside shape_hash.

loss_mask.description: Sorted list of the encoder feature coordinates the loss is computed over. Every coordinate NOT listed contributes exactly zero gradient at the head's output -- that is what the mirror-safety exclusion means mechanically.

actual_shape.description: The parameter shape createWorldMind() ACTUALLY builds, probed at load time. Post-repair (plan ant-world-mind-network-repair) the declared sizes and the built shape agree, and matches_declared is true; the probe stays pointed at reality rather than at the constants, because that is what would catch a future divergence instead of assuming one cannot happen. Both declared and actual are inside shape_hash.

prediction_head.description: 1.1 only. The world mind's learning-path prediction head (Wp: [feature count][hidden width], bp: [feature count]). Inside shape_hash: restoring a generation with no head, or a head of a different width, is silent corruption exactly as a mismatched W1 would be.

prev_features_arity.description: 1.1 only. Width of the one-tick lag carrier (prev_features). Inside shape_hash so a resize of the encoder cannot restore a stale-width lag vector.

verbs.description: Action-space ordering. Order is load-bearing: a network's output index means a verb only by position, so a reordered verb list silently remaps every learned preference.

files.description: Every authoritative state file in this generation, with its sha256 and byte size. Validation stage 4 re-hashes each one; any mismatch, any missing file, and any file present in the directory but absent from this list is a refusal. The manifest itself is never listed here -- it is the commit token, sealed by manifest_self_checksum.

path.description: Basename, relative to the generation directory. No subdirectories: a flat generation keeps the checksum sweep total and unambiguous.

input_packet.description: The frozen external decision input in force when this generation was written (world-mind-decision.json). present=false with sha256=null is the S3 default: the control arms run with no operator-console packet, so the world mind's own RNG draw is never bypassed.

goal.description: Goal fields when present. Null for every goal-free continuity control. Carried through verbatim so a goal-bearing lineage cannot silently lose its goal across a resume.

manifest_self_checksum.description: sha256 over the canonical JSON serialization of this manifest with manifest_self_checksum removed. Makes a torn or truncated manifest detectable, which is what lets manifest-arrival alone serve as the commit token.
